CELL CHECK · DEVELOPER NOTES

Connect the measurement chain.

Arduino sends calibrated readings. CellCheck records the inspection and electrical trace. Your inventory returns the next action.

Download Arduino helperDownload source code

1. Arduino serial contract

Connect over USB in a desktop browser that supports Web Serial. Use an HTTPS page (or localhost during development). The port picker requires a user click; close Arduino Serial Monitor before connecting. This interface opens at 115200 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit.

Send one UTF-8 JSON object per line, at approximately 5 Hz. CRLF is accepted. Do not mix debug text with the telemetry stream. A malformed frame invalidates an active recording and requires reconnecting.

{"type":"telemetry","battery_id":"BAT-001","seq":1,"ms":1000,"voltage":11.91,"current":1.191,"load_ohm":10,"load_active":true}
FieldMeaning
typeExactly telemetry.
battery_idMatches the selected inventory ID. 1–48 letters, digits, hyphens or underscores.
seqNonnegative integer incremented for each frame. Missing or repeated sequences invalidate a recording.
msMonotonic device timestamp in milliseconds (for example, millis()). Reconnect after a reset or timer rollover.
voltageCalibrated measured terminal voltage, in volts. JSON number.
currentCalibrated measured discharge current, in amperes. Positive for discharge; not a value calculated from voltage.
load_ohmThe resistance reported by your load subsystem, in ohms. Use null when the load is off. The interface cannot independently verify it.
load_activeBoolean reflecting the device's actual load state. Only an active load can be recorded.

The selected load must agree with the reported resistance within ±1% for capture. This is a software consistency check, not a hardware tolerance specification or safety criterion. The target voltage refers to the expected terminal voltage under the selected load and battery state; nominal pack voltage is not automatically a valid target.

Using the Arduino helper

Place CellCheckTelemetry.h next to your sketch. Include it, initialise Serial, and call the helper with your existing sensor readings:

#include "CellCheckTelemetry.h"

// In setup():
Serial.begin(115200);

// In your existing timed acquisition loop, after reading sensors:
publishCellCheckTelemetry(
    Serial,
    "BAT-001",
    measuredVoltageV,
    measuredDischargeCurrentA,
    reportedResistanceOhm,
    physicalLoadIsActive
);

The variable names above are integration placeholders, not a complete sketch. Sensor model, ADC scaling, reference voltage, pin assignments, load circuit and calibration are intentionally not assumed. Supply the actual sketch to adapt the parser or helper to its existing protocol.

Hardware responsibility

CellCheck is a read-only acquisition interface. It never writes commands to the serial port. The checklist locks recording, not the physical load. The operator must complete inspection before applying a load; firmware and hardware must independently handle limits, emergency stop, timed load removal and fault response. Stop recording, browser closure or a disconnected USB cable does not switch off the load.

The interface requires fresh, correctly identified telemetry. It rejects inactive or mismatched loads, missing samples, stale data after 3 seconds, device resets and timing drift beyond 2 seconds. It checks every recorded voltage and current sample against the configured comparison band. These software thresholds are prototype defaults, not validated protective limits.

2. Inventory API contract

Open Connections and enter an HTTPS base URL, optionally with a short-lived bearer token. Tokens remain in memory and are never written to local storage. The API must allow the deployed site's origin with CORS, including GET, POST, Content-Type and Authorization. Redirects are rejected to protect credentials. Requests time out after 10 seconds.

GET /batteries returns:

{
  "sandbox": true,
  "batteries": [{
    "id": "BAT-001",
    "name": "Robotics pack A",
    "chemistry": "LiPo",
    "cells": 3,
    "capacity": 2200,
    "location": "J18 · Cabinet A",
    "status": "needs_testing",
    "note": "Confirm the approved test profile before use.",
    "profile": {
      "voltage": 12,
      "resistance": 10,
      "tolerance": 5,
      "duration": 10
    }
  }]
}

The numbers above are illustrative. capacity is in mAh, voltage in V, resistance in Ω, tolerance in percent and duration in seconds. Profiles accept 0.1–100 V, 0.1–10,000 Ω, 0.1–20% and integer durations of 5–60 s; these are input bounds, not safe operating ranges.

POST /tests sends {"sandbox":true,"test":{...}}. The record includes a UUID, battery ID, ISO timestamp, source (arduino or simulation), kind (inspection or measurement), profile, inspection answers, all captured samples, completion state, outcome, reasons and reviewRequired:true.

The server must handle the test UUID as an idempotency key. A retry sends the same UUID so a response lost in transit does not create a duplicate. Return a JSON acknowledgement:

{
  "sandbox": true,
  "testId": "the-same-test-uuid",
  "batteryId": "BAT-001",
  "status": "needs_testing",
  "message": "Repeat the approved assessment with the responsible reviewer."
}

The acknowledgement must match the test ID, battery ID and environment. For a production API return sandbox:false; simulation uploads are blocked. The service must enforce authentication, authorisation, input validation and the same simulation restriction server-side. The prototype does not provide an inventory server.

Status codeMeaning in the interface
untestedNo screening outcome.
needs_testingIncomplete data, uncertainty or an electrical deviation. Further assessment required.
within_rangeCaptured samples meet the configured comparison bands. Human review remains required.
holdDo not test or use. A new clear checklist does not remove a hold.
approvedAn authorised decision returned by the inventory. The website never generates this from a voltage/current test. An approval response cannot override a local hold, incomplete or out-of-band test.

Only a responsible person should resolve a hold in the authoritative inventory. The approval process must consider the battery history and application; electrical readings alone do not provide a safety certification.

3. Running and extending the project

The site is buildless HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Serve dist/ from HTTPS hosting or localhost. For local development with Python, run python -m http.server 8000 --directory dist and open http://localhost:8000. Do not open the HTML as a file:// URL.

dist/app.js         Interface, recording workflow and chart
dist/engine.js      Inspection gates and assessment rules
dist/serial.js      Web Serial connection and JSON parser
dist/inventory.js   Browser persistence and REST adapter
tests/*.test.mjs    Node test suite

node --test tests/*.test.mjs

The browser inventory starts with six clearly identified example records. Add batteries, import validated JSON records, or connect an API. Exports contain both battery metadata and test history; import merges battery metadata only and preserves existing holds. API connection loads a fresh authoritative list. Local browser data is per device and is not shared storage or an authenticated approval record.

The current implementation assumes a constant-resistance load. Constant-current electronic loads need a different expected-current model. Temperature, individual cell voltage, state of charge, capacity, internal resistance, calibration uncertainty and other failure modes are not assessed here.

References and verification

  • Chrome for Developers — Web Serial API
  • Fire and Rescue NSW — damaged battery guidance
  • Fire and Rescue NSW — warning signs and emergency response

Logic, telemetry parsing and API contract checks are automated. The actual Arduino sketch, sensor hardware, production inventory and browser/device combination have not been available for end-to-end validation. The Arduino helper must be compiled and tested with your specific board and acquisition code.
